Propagated (person-to-person) epidemics show repeated peaks, each ~1 incubation period apart, e.g. measles.
Common-source outbreaks (food poisoning, typhoid) give a single sharp peak.
A district is flagged 'red' when key RMNCAH+ coverage/outcome indicators fail to cross the defined performance threshold.
Pearl Index = number of accidental pregnancies per 100 woman-years of contraceptive exposure.
Population attributable risk = the proportion of disease in the whole population attributable to (and preventable by removing) the exposure.
I²/Cochran's Q in meta-analysis quantifies statistical heterogeneity — variation in effect size between included studies.
HPV vaccine ↓es cervical cancer risk markedly but doesn't cover every oncogenic HPV type, so it can't guarantee 100% protection.
One data point per population/country (group-level exposure vs outcome) defines an ecological study.
Effectiveness = vaccine performance under real-world/routine field conditions (85%).
Efficacy = vaccine performance under ideal, controlled trial conditions (90%).
